page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.7 GHz. Its x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, AVX512 BF16, and cryptographic hardware extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource allocation includes 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. A key feature of this instance is its direct provision of 17,280 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes no dedicated GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its architectural capacity entirely toward high-throughput data processing and dense local persistence.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU throughput, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 2,083.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3,078.37, placing it in the top 25%. Geekbench multi-core performance also tests within the top 25% at 15,915.0. Memory subsystem tests report uncached large-block read bandwidth of 73.69 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 56.07 GB/sec. Across operational suites, it registered 34.48 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 22.7 GB/sec, while larger LLM inference workloads show throughput degradation due to host CPU limits on larger models.

The dense pairing of 17.28 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage and 192 GB of RAM offers strong resource density without requiring external disk attachments. Tradeoffs involve standard multi-core computing margins relative to core count and the absence of discrete hardware accelerators. Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is well configured for large NoSQL engines, distributed relational databases, data warehousing nodes, real-time analytics, and heavy transactional log ingestion.
